solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'made the hour a shared convention' is slightly loose wording; the passage speaks of noon/time, not 'the hour'
R037-01.notes: Paragraph 5 thesis: time moved from a fact about the sky to an agreement. A is a true but narrow detail (paragraph 2) and is the main trap; C overstates one reason; D contradicts paragraph 4 (no legal authority).

R037-02.notes: Boston < New York < Chicago going west, so a town farther west reaches noon still later. One-step extrapolation; some may confuse direction and pick A.

flags: minor: B (station construction cost) is a throwaway nobody would pick
R037-03.notes: Clocks each correct for some line and none for the street illustrate the confusion of per-railroad times.

flags: minor: key closely paraphrases 'trains running in opposite directions had to meet and pass at sidings' (near lookup); 'set times' is a small, reasonable inference
R037-04.notes: Opposing trains had to meet at sidings; a timing mismatch could cause a collision. A, B, D unsupported.

flags: minor: key says clocks were 'set back to noon', but the passage says only that they were 'turned back several minutes' and does not say the signal came at noon; historically accurate (the switch happened at noon on the meridian), but the passage leaves that step implicit
minor: key closely paraphrases the paragraph 3 sentence (lookup)
R037-05.notes: Towns east of the meridian were already past local noon and were turned back, so noon came twice. B reverses the direction.

flags: minor: 'missed why the change succeeded' is inferred from 'They had something more effective'; the passage never says the objectors missed this, so D is right but slightly over-specified
R037-06.notes: 'They were, in a sense, correct: the railroads had no legal authority' = agreement on the law; 'something more effective, a network' = qualification. A reverses this (it says their legal claim was mistaken) and is a strong trap for quick readers.

R037-07.notes: 'What is striking' = what is notable/remarkable. A (forceful) is the literal-sense trap.

R037-08.notes: Under standard time, noon is set by agreement, not by the sun; clocks reading noon before solar noon shows that split. A illustrates the old meaning; C is the pre-1883 confusion; D goes back to solar time.

flags: minor: slight thematic overlap with R037-01 choice D and R037-06 (railroads acted without legal authority), but no answer is given away
R037-09.notes: The 1918 date shows the public adopted standard time in practice 35 years before any law. B, C, D unsupported.
